title: chop_cells() emits a spurious empty first line when the first character is wider than max_cells
body:
## Description

`rich.cells.chop_cells()` emits a spurious empty first line when the very first character of the text is wider than `max_cells`.

## Reproduction

```python
from rich.cells import chop_cells

chop_cells("文", 1)
# actual:   ['', '文']
# expected: ['文']
```

Reproduced on rich 15.0.0 (and current `master`, `rich/cells.py`).

The root cause: the loop flushes the current (still empty) line whenever the next character does not fit. When the *first* character is a double-width CJK glyph and `max_cells` is 1, the buffer is flushed while empty, producing a leading `""` entry. Any consumer that renders line-by-line (e.g. text wrapping into width-1 or narrow columns containing CJK text) shows a blank line before the content.

Non-degenerate case for contrast — this one is already correct:

```python
chop_cells("ab文cd", 2)  # ['ab', '文', 'cd'] ✅
```

## Proposed solution

In the flush branch, only append the buffered line if it is non-empty (one-line guard). A character that can never fit still gets emitted on its own line, matching the behavior of the `"ab文cd"` case above. I have this fix ready with two regression tests (red on current master, green with the fix; full test suite passes, `black`/`mypy` clean) and can open a PR if the approach is approved, per `AI_POLICY.md`.

## Platform

Not platform-specific (pure Python, reproduced on Windows 11 / Python 3.11 / rich 15.0.0 and master).

---

*Disclosure per the spirit of `AI_POLICY.md`: this bug was found and the fix prepared with the assistance of an AI agent (Claude Code), operated and reviewed by me. If the solution is approved by a maintainer, the follow-up PR will identify itself as AI-generated as the policy requires.*

title: Docs: three broken Sphinx cross-references (verified against rich 15.0.0)
body:
### Summary

Three Sphinx `:meth:` cross-references in the docs point to symbols that do not exist, so they resolve to dead references (Sphinx: "reference target not found"). Verified against rich 15.0.0 on Python 3.14.

1. `docs/source/markup.rst` lines 103 and 105 use `:meth:`~rich.console.Print.print``. There is no `Print` class in `rich.console`; the method is `Console.print`. Suggested fix: `:meth:`~rich.console.Console.print``.
2. `docs/source/console.rst` line 368 uses `:meth:`~rich.ScreenContext.update``. `ScreenContext` lives at `rich.console.ScreenContext`, not `rich.ScreenContext`. Suggested fix: `:meth:`~rich.console.ScreenContext.update``.

Repro:
- `python -c "import rich.console as c; c.Print"` -> AttributeError (no `Print`)
- `python -c "import rich; rich.ScreenContext"` -> AttributeError (no `rich.ScreenContext`)
- Correct targets exist under `.. automodule:: rich.console`: `Console.print` and `ScreenContext.update`.

These were found with AI assistance (Claude) and I verified each against the installed rich 15.0.0. Per `AI_POLICY.md`, I am opening this issue first rather than sending a PR directly. If a maintainer confirms the fix is wanted, I am happy to submit a small PR correcting all three references.

title: [BUG] set_cell_size returns incorrect result for negative total with narrow text
body:
- [x] I've checked [docs](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html) and [closed issues](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) for possible solutions. 
- [x] I can't find my issue in the [FAQ](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/master/FAQ.md).

**Describe the bug**

`set_cell_size()` returns incorrectly truncated text when `total` is negative and the input consists entirely of single-cell-width characters.

For example:

```python
from rich.cells import set_cell_size

print(repr(set_cell_size("ab", -1)))
print(repr(set_cell_size("abc", -1)))
print(repr(set_cell_size("abcdef", -1)))
```

Currently this produces:

```
'a'
'ab'
'abcde'
```

Expected:

```
''
''
''
```

The issue is caused by the `total <= 0` guard being placed after the single-cell-width fast path:

```python
if _is_single_cell_widths(text):
    size = len(text)
    if size < total:
        return text + " " * (total - size)
    return text[:total]

if total <= 0:
    return ""
```

For single-cell-width strings, negative slicing is therefore reached before the guard. Python's negative slicing causes part of the string to be returned.

For comparison, strings containing wide characters correctly return an empty string because they do not take the single-cell-width fast path.

The fix is to move the `total <= 0` check before the `_is_single_cell_widths()` fast path.

I have also added regression tests covering negative `total` values.

**Platform**

- macOS
- Python 3.13.6

The issue is reproducible independently of terminal software.

I have already implemented the fix and added regression tests in my fork. I would be happy to submit the changes as a pull request if I can be granted contributor access, or I can follow whatever contribution process you prefer.

title: Console.print(text) silently drops Text's own justify unless justify= is also passed to print()
body:
**AI disclosure (per AI_POLICY.md):** this was investigated and written with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic). I independently reproduced it against a fresh clone of `main` myself before filing — repro below, runnable standalone, no dependencies beyond Rich itself.

## Summary

A `Text` object's own `.justify` attribute is silently dropped when the `Text` is passed directly as a top-level argument to `Console.print()`, unless `justify=` is *also* passed to `print()` itself — even though `Text.__rich_console__` documents/implements `self.justify` as taking priority over the console-level default.

## Reproduction

```python
from rich.console import Console
from rich.text import Text
import io

buf1 = io.StringIO()
Console(file=buf1, width=20).print(Text("hi", justify="center"))
print(repr(buf1.getvalue()))
# -> 'hi\n'                    <- not centered, despite Text's own justify="center"

buf2 = io.StringIO()
Console(file=buf2, width=20).print(Text("hi", justify="center"), justify="center")
print(repr(buf2.getvalue()))
# -> '         hi         \n'  <- only works if justify is ALSO passed to print()
```

## Root cause

`Console._collect_renderables()` (`rich/console.py:1550-1554`, inside `check_text()`) funnels every `Text` object through:
```python
sep_text = Text(sep, justify=justify, end=end)   # justify = print()'s own kwarg, default None
append(sep_text.join(text))
```
`Text.join()` (`rich/text.py:788`) builds the merged result via `self.blank_copy()`, where `self` is the *separator* `sep_text` — so the joined result inherits the **separator's** `justify`/`overflow`/`no_wrap`, silently clobbering whatever the joined-in `Text`'s own `.justify` was set to.

The same `Text` object centers correctly when wrapped in `Panel(...)` or `Group(...)`, because those containers call `console.render()` on the inner `Text` directly, bypassing this join path — so the bug is specific to passing a `Text` as a direct top-level argument to `Console.print()`.

title: [BUG] Console tests fail when COLUMNS or LINES is exported in the shell
body:
- [x] I've checked docs and closed issues for possible solutions.
- [x] I can't find my issue in the FAQ.

**Describe the bug**

Running the test suite in a shell that exports `COLUMNS` (as CI systems and some terminal multiplexers do) makes 6 tests in `tests/test_console.py` fail, because the environment takes precedence over the mocked terminal size:

```
COLUMNS=200 LINES=50 python -m pytest tests/test_console.py -p no:randomly
```

```
FAILED tests/test_console.py::test_size_can_fall_back_to_std_descriptors[False-ValueError-ValueError-ValueError-ValueError-expected_size5]
  assert (200, 50) == (80, 25)
6 failed, 94 passed
```

Without the variables exported the same file passes 100/100. I checked this in a controlled comparison (32 runs with the variables exported vs 32 without, with hash seed, timezone and locale also varied as controls): 0/32 pass exported, 32/32 pass clean, and none of the control factors move the result.

The library behavior is intentional (`Console.__init__` reads `COLUMNS` and `LINES` from `self._environ`, rich/console.py around line 685). The tests just never isolate themselves from the inherited environment, while other test files already do: `tests/test_tree.py` and `tests/test_logging.py` construct their consoles with `_environ={}` for exactly this reason.

**Proposed fix**

Pass `_environ={}` to the `Console` instances in the affected `tests/test_console.py` tests (or scrub `COLUMNS`/`LINES` with an autouse monkeypatch fixture for that file). Happy to send a PR if that direction works for you.

**Platform**

Reproduced on macOS (arm64), Python 3.13, pytest 9.1.1, at master 9d8f9a3; the mechanism only depends on the inherited environment, so it should not be platform-specific.

_Investigated with the help of Claude (Anthropic's Claude Code)._

**Describe the bug**

`tests/test_table.py::test_placement_table_box_elements` builds a `Table` with the module-level `box.ASCII` singleton and then rewrites that singleton in place (`table.box.__dict__.update(...)`, tests/test_table.py line 314) without restoring it. def test_get_row():

>   assert row == "|-+--+---|"
E   AssertionError: assert 'ijkjjkjjjl' == '|-+--+---|'

The suite only stays green because the natural file order happens to run test_box.py before test_table.py. Under pytest-randomly (which the test environment installs) the polluter runs first on roughly half the seeds: in a controlled comparison of 48 shuffled runs against 48 with the plugin disabled, the shuffled runs passed 52% and the natural order 100%, with hash seed, timezone, locale and allocator varied as controls that all stayed quiet.

title: [BUG] Traceback rendering fails on ParseError with a non-string message
body:
- [x] Checked the traceback documentation and searched open/closed issues for `SyntaxError`, `ParseError`, and `ExpatError`.
- [x] Checked the FAQ.

**Describe the bug**

Rendering an `xml.etree.ElementTree.ParseError` whose message is an `ExpatError` raises a secondary `TypeError`, masking the original XML parse error. This occurs with the pure-Python ElementTree parser used by defusedxml (see tiran/defusedxml#105). The reproduction below needs only Rich and the standard library:

```python
import io
import sys
from xml.etree.ElementTree import ParseError
from xml.parsers.expat import ExpatError

from rich.console import Console
from rich.traceback import Traceback

try:
    raise ParseError(ExpatError("syntax error"))
except ParseError:
    Console(file=io.StringIO()).print(Traceback.from_exception(*sys.exc_info()))
```

Actual result:

```text
TypeError: str or Text instance required, not ExpatError('syntax error')
```

Expected: render the original exception without raising a new exception.

`ParseError` subclasses `SyntaxError`. `Traceback.extract()` currently stores `exc_value.msg` directly in `_SyntaxError`, although it already has a `safe_str()` helper for the main exception value. Would normalizing this field with that helper, with tests for non-string messages and a failing `__str__`, be an acceptable fix?

**Platform**

macOS arm64, CPython 3.13.5, Rich 15.0.0. Also reproduced using the current `main` checkout. Output is directed to `StringIO`, so no terminal-specific rendering is involved. The original end-to-end example also fails with defusedxml 0.8.0rc2 and structlog 26.1.0. Explicitly selecting `structlog.dev.plain_traceback` is a verified workaround for that integration.

This report and local reproduction were prepared with OpenAI Codex. Per the AI policy, no PR is being submitted without maintainer approval of the proposed solution.

title: highlight_words([]) creates zero-length matches
body:
### Description

`Text.highlight_words()` treats an empty word iterable as an empty regular expression. Python's regex engine then finds zero-width matches at every character boundary, so the method reports false matches and appends zero-length spans.

### Steps to reproduce

```python
from rich.text import Text

text = Text("abc")
count = text.highlight_words([], "red")

assert count == 0
assert text._spans == []
```

### Expected behavior

An empty word list should be a no-op and return `0`.

### Actual behavior

The current implementation builds `re_words = ""` and `re.finditer("", "abc")` yields four zero-width matches. `highlight_words()` returns `4` and appends four zero-length spans.

The implementation is in `rich/text.py`, and existing tests only cover non-empty word iterables. I searched existing issues and pull requests for `highlight_words([])` and did not find a matching report.

Would maintainers accept a small guard for an empty word iterable plus a regression test? The repository's contribution guide requires tests and a changelog entry for a bug fix.

**The bug**

`Text.from_ansi` exposes OSC 8 payload text and loses the link when the sequence ends with BEL. The equivalent ST-terminated sequence works.

```python
from rich.text import Text

for terminator in ("\x1b\\", "\x07"):
    source = f"\x1b]8;;https://example.com{terminator}hello\x1b]8;;{terminator}"
    text = Text.from_ansi(source)
    print(repr(text.plain), [(s.start, s.end, str(s.style)) for s in text.spans])
```

Actual output:

```text
'hello' [(0, 5, 'link https://example.com')]
'8;;https://example.comhello8;;' []
```

Expected: both inputs produce plain text `hello` with the same link span. Xterm documents both BEL and ST as OSC terminators: https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html#h3-Operating-System-Commands

`re_ansi` in `rich/ansi.py` currently recognizes ST for its OSC branch, but not BEL. This is distinct from #3561, which measures raw ANSI strings without converting them first.

**Platform**

Current main commit `9d8f9a3`, Python 3.14.6, macOS arm64. Reproduced from the checkout with markdown-it-py and Pygments installed via uv. No terminal rendering is needed to reproduce this.

AI assistance (Codex) was used to investigate and prepare this report; the output above was verified locally. No PR is attached.

title: [BUG] Text.from_ansi: NUL byte between ESC and "[" bypasses re_ansi and reaches the terminal as a live escape sequence
body:
- [x] I've checked [docs](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html) and [closed issues](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) for possible solutions.
- [x] I can't find my issue in the [FAQ](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/master/FAQ.md).

**Platform**
Tested against rich v15.0.0 with kali's default terminal, qterminal.

**Describe the bug**
`Text.from_ansi` uses re_ansi to tokenize ANSI escape sequences. The regex expects ESC (0x1B) to be immediately followed by a recognized byte, so a NUL (0x00) inserted between ESC and "[" prevents a match. `_ansi_tokenize` then yields the whole sequence as a literal plain-text token.

`Text.append()` passes it through `strip_control_codes()`, but that only strips codes 7, 8, 11, 12 and 13, not NUL (0) or ESC (27). The raw ESC NUL [2J bytes therefore survive in the Text and are printed. Many terminal emulators ignore NUL bytes, so they reconstruct and execute the sequence.

**PoC**
(Note: This will erase the entire terminal. Ensure your terminal has text on the screen to observe the clear-screen command)
```
from rich.text import Text
msg = "\x1b\x00[2J"
text = Text.from_ansi(msg)
print(text)
```

**Impact**
Tools that pass untrusted data (e.g. file contents from a network share) through from_ansi can emit unintended control sequences: screen clearing, cursor movement, and output spoofing.

**Suggested fix**
The regex could account for NUL after ESC, and `strip_control_codes` could be extended to also strip NUL bytes that survive outside of a successfully matched sequence, as defense in depth.

title: [BUG] Text.wrap(console, width=0) raises ValueError in chop_cells (range step 0)
body:
**Describe the bug**

`Text.wrap(console, width=0)` raises `ValueError: range() arg 3 must not be zero` for ordinary (single-cell) text. The same call with double-width text does not crash, so the behaviour is inconsistent.

The crash is in `rich/cells.py::chop_cells`, whose single-cell fast path builds `range(0, len(text), width)`:

```python
if _is_single_cell_widths(text):
    return [text[index : index + width] for index in range(0, len(text), width)]
```

With `width == 0` the step is `0`, which `range` rejects. The general (wide-character) path below it has no such step and returns without raising, so `chop_cells("hello", 0)` crashes while `chop_cells("你好", 0)` does not.

It reaches the public API through `Text.wrap` -> `_wrap.divide_line` -> `chop_cells` (the `word_length > width` fold branch, taken by any non-empty word when `width` is 0). Width 0 is reachable when text is rendered into a zero-interior region (a table column squeezed to zero, a nested panel with no room, a console sized to 0); Rich otherwise degrades gracefully at tiny widths, so a hard crash here stands out.

**Minimal repro** (runs as-is):

```python
import io
from rich.console import Console
from rich.text import Text

console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
Text("hello world").wrap(console, 0)   # ValueError: range() arg 3 must not be zero
```

Lower-level, showing the single-cell vs wide-char inconsistency:

```python
from rich._wrap import divide_line
divide_line("hello", 0)   # ValueError: range() arg 3 must not be zero
divide_line("你好", 0)     # returns normally
```

title: [BUG] Text negative integer indexing drops span styles
body:
- [x] I've checked the docs and closed issues for possible solutions.
- [x] I can't find my issue in the FAQ.

**Describe the bug**

Indexing styled `Text` with a negative integer returns the correct character but loses its spans. Positive indexing and a negative slice preserve the style. Python's negative-index semantics suggest `text[-1]` should be equivalent to `text[len(text) - 1]`, including formatting.

```python
from rich.text import Text

text = Text.from_markup("[bold]hello[/bold]")
print(text[4].plain, text[4].spans)
print(text[-1].plain, text[-1].spans)
print(text[-3:].plain, text[-3:].spans)
```

Actual output:

```text
o [Span(0, 1, 'bold')]
o []
llo [Span(0, 3, 'bold')]
```

Expected: `text[-1]` returns a bold `o` like `text[4]`.

At `rich/text.py:198-209`, `__getitem__` uses the negative offset for Python string indexing (which succeeds), but compares that same negative offset with nonnegative span boundaries (which never match). Indexing once to keep Python's `IndexError` behavior and then normalizing the negative offset before checking spans appears to fix it. Could @willmcgugan confirm that preserving spans for negative integer indices is the intended behavior? I have not opened a PR pending the approval required by `AI_POLICY.md`.

**Platform**

Windows, CPython 3.10.1, Rich 15.0.0 installed editable from default-branch commit `9d8f9a372cc5916fd4781fec207ced7ddac2f08f`. Pure API example; terminal rendering not required. Searched open and closed issues/PRs for negative Text indexes and lost styles without finding a matching report.

title: [BUG] Traceback.extract loops forever when __cause__ and __context__ form a cycle
body:
- [x] I've checked [docs](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html) and [closed issues](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) for possible solutions.
- [x] I can't find my issue in the [FAQ](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/master/FAQ.md).

**Describe the bug**

`Traceback.extract` loops forever when an exception chain forms a cycle through `__cause__` and `__context__`.

`Traceback.extract` follows `__cause__`, then `__context__`, until neither is set. It guards only against an exception that is its own cause (the fix for #3708) and against repeated exception-group members. So when two or more exceptions form a cycle, for example A's `__context__` is B and B's `__cause__` is A, the loop never ends. `stacks` grows by one entry per pass and memory grows without bound. `Console.print_exception()`, `Traceback.from_exception(...)` and `RichHandler(rich_tracebacks=True)` never return.

Ordinary code builds such a chain: re-raising an exception with `raise error` inside the handler of an exception that was raised `from` it. When Python sets `__context__`, it breaks cycles that run only through `__context__` links, but not cycles that pass through `__cause__`. The chain is legal, and the standard library prints it, because `traceback.TracebackException` keeps a `_seen` set and prints each exception once.

Minimal example (runs unmodified):

```python
import traceback

from rich.console import Console

error = ValueError("inner")
try:
    try:
        try:
            raise error
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError("outer") from exc
    except RuntimeError:
        raise error  # error.__context__ is the RuntimeError, whose __cause__ is error
except ValueError:
    traceback.print_exc()  # the standard library prints the chain and returns
    print("stdlib done", flush=True)
    Console().print_exception()  # rich never returns
    print("rich done", flush=True)
```

**Expected:** rich prints e

**Describe the bug**

Printing a `Panel` (or any wrapped `Text`) that contains certain zero-width-joiner strings at a narrow width crashes with `IndexError: list index out of range`. This is on current master (`9d8f9a3`).

```python
from rich.console import Console
from rich.panel import Panel
from rich.text import Text

zwj = chr(0x200D)  # zero-width joiner
Console(width=10).print(Panel(Text(zwj + zwj + "👩界क�a👩"), expand=True, padding=0))
```

```
rich/text.py:880 in truncate

rich/cells.py:322 in set_cell_size
    text, _ = _split_text(text, total, unicode_version)
rich/cells.py:266 in _split_text
    start, end, cell_size = spans[offset]
IndexError: list index out of range

`cell_len` counts each codepoint, but `split_graphemes` groups zero-width-joiner sequences into single (sometimes zero-width) graphemes, so the two can disagree: for the string above `cell_len` is 9 while the graphemes span only 7 cells. `set_cell_size` sees 9 > 8 and calls `_split_text(text, 8)`, whose walk then runs past the last span: the `left_size < cell_position` branch has no `offset >= len(spans)` guard.

Minimal direct repro: `_split_text("👩" + chr(0x200D) + "💻", 6)` raises `IndexError` (the grapheme spans 2 cells, position 6 is beyond it).

When the walk passes the last span, the whole string fits left of the requested position, so return `(text, "")`:

title: [BUG] Three workflows still point at the master branch, so CodeQL and the FAQ bot have been dead since the rename
body:
- [x] I've checked [docs](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html) and [closed issues](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) for possible solutions.
- [x] I can't find my issue in the FAQ.

**Describe the bug**

Three workflow files still name `master`. Since the rename to `main` they point at a branch that does not exist, so two of them never trigger and one fails on every run.

This is not the `blob/master` link nitpick from #4204. Those are web URLs and GitHub redirects them. `git fetch` and the Actions `branches:` filter resolve a ref by exact name under `refs/heads` and do not follow that redirect, which is why these three are broken while the links keep working.

`git ls-remote --heads https://github.com/Textualize/rich.git` returns a single head, `refs/heads/main`. There is no `master`.

**`.github/workflows/newissue.yml:13`, `ref: master`**

`actions/checkout` runs `fetch ... +refs/heads/master*:refs/remotes/origin/master*`, matches nothing, retries twice and exits 1. The five steps after it are skipped, so no FAQ suggestion is posted on a new issue. Last green run 2026-06-14, first failure 2026-06-16, 47 consecutive failures through 2026-10-18.

**`.github/workflows/codeql.yml:5` and `:8`, `branches: [ 'master' ]`**

The last `push` run was 2026-04-12 and the last `pull_request` run 2026-05-23. Everything since is the Friday `schedule`. #4175 is the only pull request merged after the rename, and its checks are 17 `build` jobs and two `codespell` runs, with no CodeQL among them.

**`.github/workflows/readmechanged.yml:6`, `- master`**

It did not fire for #4175, which changed `README.md` on `main`. The only run in its retained history is 2025-12-22.

The workflows that declare no branch filter are unaffected, which is why `comment.yml` sits at 0 failures while `newissue.yml` is at 47: `pythonpackage.yml`, `codespell.yml`, `comment.yml`.

**The fix**

`master` to `main` on those four lines.
